statement: Build a one-file website for CityCare Hospital, Bengaluru, where patients can send a visit request, find emergency information, browse doctor profiles and read a health blog, in English, Kannada and Hindi.
audience: Patients and their families in Bengaluru who read English, Kannada or Hindi, often on a phone and sometimes in an urgent situation.
standards: Plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript in one file, no build step, CDN libraries allowed.
Mobile-first and readable on a small screen, with labeled form fields and sufficient text contrast.
Emergency information is easy to find at the top of the page and is never hidden behind a menu or a language change.
Any fact not supplied in the brief is shown as a clearly marked placeholder, never as plausible sample data.
Health wording is plain and short in all three languages.
rules: Use only facts from the brief or the Requester. Do not invent phone numbers, addresses, doctor names, credentials, hours or medical claims.
No backend and no live slot availability. Booking is a visit request that opens a prefilled WhatsApp or email message, and staff confirm each visit by hand.
Blog posts are labeled general information, not medical advice.
Kannada and Hindi pages show a visible pending native-speaker review note.
The site does not store or transmit patient data except through the message the patient chooses to send.
Missing facts and reviews are tracked as open inputs and do not block done.
done_when: The site is a single HTML file with its CSS and JavaScript inline or loaded from a CDN, and needs no build step or backend.
A language switcher offers English, Kannada and Hindi, and every visible section, including emergency and booking, has text in all three.
The Kannada and Hindi views each show a visible note that the translation is pending native-speaker review.

An emergency section sits at the top of the page and shows a marked placeholder for the hospital emergency number and address, plus a line telling users to call their local emergency number, in all three languages.
A visit-request form has name, phone, preferred doctor, date and time fields, and submitting it opens a prefilled WhatsApp or email message to the hospital.
Near the form, the text states that there is no live slot availability and that staff confirm each visit by hand, in all three languages.
A doctor profiles section shows cards whose names and credentials are marked placeholders, with no invented doctor data.
A health blog section lists posts, each labeled as general information, not medical advice, in all three languages.
The hospital WhatsApp number and email address are clearly named placeholder constants in the script, and no real-looking contact value appears anywhere in the file.
open_inputs: Hospital street address and map location
Hospital WhatsApp number and email address for visit requests
Doctor names, specialties and credentials, and photos if wanted
Blog article text, or confirmation of which topics to publish
Native-speaker review of Kannada and Hindi text, emergency and booking wording first
